blocks.heading: Compare the Practical Paths
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Career after BA history India: 9 real paths, compared

rows: Law through CLAT
Graduates who found the political and legal history sections more engaging than the rest of the syllabus.

CLAT has no age limit and unlimited attempts. Top NLU graduates can start above Rs 15-18 LPA; tier-2 and tier-3 law college outcomes are far more modest. Independent practice later on is a genuine ownership path with no fixed pay ceiling.
Corporate and generalist roles (content, HR, business analysis)
Graduates who want faster, non-exam entry into stable private-sector income.

History alone rarely opens these doors. A multiplier skill (writing systems, data basics, communication training) has to sit on top of the degree, but the pay ceiling here is often the highest of all nine paths once you specialise.
Journalism, publishing, and documentary research
Graduates who write well and want their history knowledge to show up as public work, not a filing cabinet of facts.

Entry-level reporter, editorial, and documentary-research roles typically start around Rs 2.5-5 LPA. A visible portfolio matters more than a mass-communication credential, and freelance or own-byline work can scale well beyond a single employer's pay band.
Heritage tourism and guiding
Graduates who like direct public interaction and storytelling more than desk-bound research.
The Ministry of Tourism runs a formal 330-hour Heritage Tour Guide certification and a 420-hour Regional Level Guide course, open to candidates 18-28 with at least Class 10.
Museums and heritage management
Graduates drawn to objects, exhibitions, and public-facing interpretation of the past.
Entry-level assistant curator roles typically pay roughly Rs 30,000-45,000 a month; senior curator and director roles can reach Rs 1.5-3 lakh a month over a full career.
Archaeology (ASI, state departments)
Graduates who want fieldwork, excavation, and material evidence, not only archival paperwork.
Needs a specific MA (Ancient History and Archaeology, or History plus a PG Diploma in Archaeology). Selection runs through written exams, skill tests, and interviews.

blocks.heading: Real Cost and Timeline Map
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The real cost and timeline map

rows: BA History (3 or 4 years depending on your university's structure)
The starting point for every path below, not the finish line for most of them.
MA History with the right specialisation (Modern Indian History, Ancient History and Archaeology, or Museology)
Typically 2 more years, and the specific specialisation genuinely changes which government exam or job posting you become eligible for.
Diploma in Archival Studies or PG Diploma in Archaeology, where required
Usually a further 1 year on top of the MA, specific to the archives or archaeology tracks.
UPSC or State PSC preparation, if you go the civil services route
Coaching and materials commonly run Rs 1.5-3 lakh per prep year, before rent and living costs in a coaching hub, on top of foregone income of roughly Rs 4-6 lakh a year.
PhD via UGC NET JRF or an ICHR fellowship, if you go the research or academia route
3 or more years, funded at roughly Rs 37,000-42,000 a month (UGC NET JRF) or roughly Rs 17,600 a month (ICHR JRF), depending on which fellowship you clear.

figures.source: Fresh reporter and editorial roles typically start around Rs 2.5-5 LPA. blocks.heading: Museums and Heritage Management

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Entry-level assistant curator roles typically pay roughly Rs 30,000-45,000 a month, mid-level curator or gallery-manager roles Rs 60,000-90,000, and senior director-level roles Rs 1.5-3 lakh a month or more. INTACH, state museums, and private heritage trusts are the main hiring bodies alongside government museums.

blocks.heading: Teaching and Research: NET, JRF, and ICHR

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: UGC NET JRF pays roughly Rs 37,000 a month for the first two years, rising to about Rs 42,000 as a Senior Research Fellow. ICHR's own Junior Research Fellowship for history PhD scholars pays less, around Rs 17,600 a month plus a small annual contingency grant, awarded through its own entrance exam and interview. Government college assistant professor basic pay starts near Rs 57,700 (roughly Rs 90,000-1.1 lakh gross with allowances); private colleges commonly pay Rs 40,000-60,000 for the same designation.

items.text: Do you want fieldwork or desk work.
